why: The edits only add prefetch={false} to links named by file and line, and the lines match the code. Removing a prefetch cannot break where a link goes, so the worst outcome of a missed or extra link is a speed difference. The one weak point is the new e2e spec: if it misreads the prefetch header names it counts 0 prefetches and passes without testing anything. That only weakens a speed guard and touches nothing sensitive.
harm_if_wrong: A link is still prefetched (wasted requests), or the new prefetch spec passes without measuring anything.
brief_problems: In site-parts.tsx the brief says to find 'the withdrawal and legal links drawn in this file' with rg -n 'withdraw|legalPages|page\.href' and give each the attribute. That rg leads to line 282-283, the platform's legalPages links, which the same paragraph says to leave alone (283, 287). In this file the store's withdrawal link is WithdrawalLink from store-layout.tsx (already covered), and no store legal-page link is drawn here, so the sentence should be deleted.
Case (4) of the spec (no stylesheet after load on four pages) tests something none of the edits change. If it fails for an unrelated reason, the cheap model stops.
